about: By hand: the abbreviation lawyers cite an instrument by where its own source gives none. A BWB regulation or treaty has its abbreviations in its WTI (`afkortingen`) and needs no entry; EUR-Lex gives an EU act a short title in words (`algemene verordening gegevensbescherming`), never the abbreviation. An entry is keyed by the BWB id or CELEX number of the instrument and counts only while that instrument is in the graph; a source abbreviation of another instrument wins over it. `lawgraph curated set instrument-abbreviations`.
